answer: At pressing time every bushel is weighed at the cider mill, and the press master writes the weight in his book before the screw turns. Dyer apprenticeship certificate with trade guild attestation is the press book's authority: three-year apprenticeship, 4,000 supervised hours, practical exam, guild dues. A bushel smuggled in under a false onyx is found when the juice runs short. The summit is the penalty, the whole pressing forfeited to the orchard owner, and the crystal is the mill ledger, kept in the press house and settled at Michaelmas.
